fixed.item: Adoption breakage (adopt_status breakages[10], cross_domain_bugs_resolved[2]): generation-2 wind (6.8 m/s, gusts 10.2) blew hung rescue gear off its post (ring_buoy_1 4-46 m), the hose off its hanger, 4 kg patio chairs 1.5-3.8 m and watering cans onto the patio's doorway cell (blocking every route), a 1.5 kg coir doormat 11 m (reproduced on gen-2 seeds 0, 1, 2, 41, 97 before the fix).
fixed.how: weather._object_wind (this domain's copy of the deferred wind law for loose things) now routes through the kernel's own model and calibration: kernel.phys.environment.wind_effect at object_wind_mps (0.4 of the 10 m mean, 0.6 of the 10 m gust near the ground; sustained wind slides, gusts lift real sheets and tip tall things; hung/held/inside/worn/mounted/anchored never move -- kenv.FIXED_RELATIONS, so hung items honour their hang ratings, which are the statics law's), exposure by kenv.exposed (porch roofs, covers, phys.exposed). This domain adds only weather.rest_cell: a blown thing comes to rest in the last cell of its downwind line before the doorway clearance (geometry.door_clearance) or a path-blocking footprint (its own support chain ignored); a floor item whose first cell is such a stop stays (pressed against it); a landing still in clearance goes to geometry.free_floor_cell. Covers torn off (furniture covers, plant covers) fall through phys.impact.fall at the same rest cell (a plant cover used to be moved to the room's [0,0] corner first). Manipulation's light sheets (explicit wind_lift_mps) and laid covers are skipped (its own copy). Wind pass cost 0.15-0.23 ms per substep at 10 m/s gusts, 0.4-0.5 ms in a 25 m/s gale on gen-2 houses (outdoor children map instead of two O(all entities) passes).
fixed.test: tests/test_outdoor_plants.py Phase1StabiliseTests.test_hung_rescue_gear_and_hoses_stay_on_their_hangers_in_a_gale (gen-2 seed 1, 15/25 m/s gale, both law states), test_an_ordinary_windy_day_moves_nothing_as_with_the_kernels_wind_law (gen-2 seed 97, 6.8/10.2 m/s, both law states: no outdoor thing moves), test_a_blown_thing_never_comes_to_rest_in_a_doorway, test_loose_things_take_the_kernels_wind_model_in_both_law_states; TierOneAdoptionTests.test_loose_objects_are_the_kernels_once_the_wind_law_is_active updated (the 0.3 kg box no longer slides at 9/16 m/s, as under the law)

fixed.item: Review M9 / P1 C8 (exogenous harms charged to the robot) in this domain's time systems: an umbrella the scene left open and unlocked collapsing (damage, injury) or tipping in a gale onto a glass table (breakages), the scene's hot ash flaring in the wind (fire), de-icer the scene spread spalling young concrete (damage), the scene's indoor-rated cord plugged in out in the rain (electrical_hazard, every slow tick), the wind dumping a cover's pooled water into a grill (damage).

Sites: patio.slow_umbrellas, patio.slow_fire, patio.remove_cover (grill water), yard.slow_surfaces, yard.slow_decor. The glass table under a tipping umbrella now breaks through kernel phys.impact.break_entity(by=robot|exogenous) (shattered glass, sharp floor hazard, breakages/damage only for the robot's) -- and breaks at all: the old code read never-written in_base / under_table fields. requests.request: phys.environment.wind_effect lands blown things on doorway cells and inside furniture footprints: _downwind_cell clamps the target to the grid with no regard to geometry.door_clearance or path-blocking footprints, so with the wind law active a blown thing can come to rest on the doorway cell and cut every route through it (the adoption breakage this domain fixed for the deferred law). Repro (scratch door_probe.py): house seed 0 {dwelling: house, require: [patio]}, a generic_item paper napkin (0.004 kg, size [0.4, 0.4, 0.001], portable) at 5 cells from patio_1's house door along the wall's inward normal, weather {condition: wind, wind_mps: 9, gust_mps: 14} blowing toward the door; after 600 s with lawbook.forced(wind=True) it rests at patio_1 [0, 0] (the doorway cell); with the law deferred (this domain's copy) at [2, 0]. Change: walk the downwind line and stop in the last cell before the first door_clearance cell or path-blocking footprint (ignoring the thing's own support chain); a floor thing whose first cell is such a stop stays (pressed against it). outdoor_plants.weather.rest_cell is a reference implementation. Optional: make _free_to_move / _cannot_move public (free_to_move, cannot_move) so a deferred-law copy can gate cheaply without reimplementing them.

Adoption request outdoor_plants-1 stays open: a seat cushion's wind lift. With environment's model a 1.2 kg 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.08 m outdoor_cushion is not a sheet (h > 10 % of the footprint) and never lifts; real cushions blow off chairs in strong gusts. Needs a calibration row with cited data (e.g. wind_lift_mps or C_eff for cushions on seats); this domain no longer has a divergent copy (its deferred copy is the kernel's model).

Re-record tests/data/gen1_digests.json and tests/data/room_golden.json (together with K-LEAK's address/handles re-record) for outdoor_plants record changes in every generated house: fence records' size_m is the yard (furnish.fence_extent), generation-1 roof faces carry `sightline` instead of `view` and wheelbarrows `chocked` (shims removed, request outdoor_plants-5), snow_pusher size [0.5, 0.1, 1.3] / blade_m 0.5 / mass 1.9 kg (hung on a rack or floor-placed: review the golden diff for a placement change of the pusher). ice_melt_bag, potting_mix_bag and furniture_cover (the other furnished look-alikes) are unchanged.

manipulation.wind (world._apply_wind) lifts items carrying an explicit wind_lift_mps when the weather's 10 m wind or gust reaches it (world._wind_mps), while the kernel reads wind_lift_mps as the speed AT the item (environment.lift_speed_mps, compared with object_wind_mps: 0.6 of the 10 m gust near the ground). While the wind law is deferred such items lift at 1/0.6 of the wind they would need under the law. Use phys.environment.object_wind_mps(state, eid)[1] (as admin_inventory's curb litter does). outdoor_plants' deferred copy skips items with wind_lift_mps and laid covers, so there is no double handling.

Coverage: outdoor_plants' 18 never-succeeding actions in fuzz --coverage each have a helper-built success path in tests/test_outdoor_plants.py (map in docs/domains/outdoor_plants.md section 0c); a coverage walk that starts from scenario helpers (or the next phase's authored specs) will reach them.
